title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: RGenEDA designed provide streamlined, unified reproducible framework exploratory data analysis across multiple omics data types. vignette introduces key components RGenEDA package using bulk RNA-seq data paper Genomewide binding transcription factor Snail1 triple-negative breast cancer cell (Maturi, et al. 2018). Raw counts metadata obtained Gene Expression Atlas ENA:ERP019920, E-MTAB-5244. data pre-wrangled standard deseq2 framework applied demonstrate functionality RGenEDA. paper explores epithelial cell line HS578T. authors introduced knock-Snail1 transcription factor compare wild-type (WT) HS578T cells.

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: standard DESeq2 workflow can now applied. end goal obtain normalized counts differential expression results. Lowly expressed genes filtered running DESeq2.
code: # Ensure tables are not scrambled all(colnames(counts) == rownames(metadata)) #> [1] TRUE  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(   countData = counts,   colData = metadata,   design = ~ Genotype ) #> Warning in DESeqDataSet(se, design = design, ignoreRank): some variables in #> design formula are characters, converting to factors  # Set reference levels dds$Genotype <- relevel(dds$Genotype, ref = "WT")  # Pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in  at least 3 samples keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3 dds <- dds[keep,]  # Run DESeq2 dds <- DESeq(dds)  # Rlog transform the data and extract normalized matrix rld <- rlog(dds) mat <- assay(rld)

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: normalized counts metadata prepared, GenEDA object can initialized. object store components analysis, starting normalized data metadata (bare minimum requirements). see object also contains slots Highly Variable Genes (HVGs), DimReduction (PCA, etc..) Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs). populated shortly RGenEDA
code: # Factor metadata metadata$Genotype <- factor(metadata$Genotype, levels = c("WT", "Snai1_KO"))  # Initialize GenEDA object with normalized counts and metadata obj <- GenEDA(   normalized = mat,   metadata = metadata)  # View object summary obj #> geneda object #>   features: 11247 #>   samples:  6 #>   HVGs: 0 #>   DimReduction: 0 #>   counts: NULL #>   DEGs: none

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: visualize normalized count distributions across samples, PlotCountDist() function can used. quick helpful way visualize effectiveness normalization, overall distributions similar across samples. Samples low high overall counts compared others might indicate problematic samples, technical artifacts, batch effect. function returns ggplot2 object facilitate additional customization.
code: PlotCountDist(obj, split_by = "Genotype")

what: Sample Eucliden distances with hierarchical clustering
title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: visualize replicate similarity, Euclidean distances samples can calculated plotted pheatmap heatmap using PlotDistances() function. Darker colors indicate higher similarity, lighter colors represent dissimilar samples. provides quick assessment replicate quality metadata features drive clustering. save pheatmap objects within RGenEDA, can use GenSave() function, similar function ggsave().
code: hm <- PlotDistances(   obj,   meta_cols = c("Genotype"),   palettes = colorList,   return = "plot" ) hm$heatmap  # GenSave(hm, "/path/to/EuclidenDistance_Heatmap.png", width = 6, height = 8)

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: Next, genes ranked decreasing variance find highly variable genes (HVGs) -likely drive biological differences. full variance profile curve genes profiled plotHVGVariance() means pick meaningful number HVGs retain calculating principal components next section. what: Explore Eigen vectors of individual PCs
title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: individual Eigenvectors (genes) comprise particular component interest can extracted Z-scaled normalized expression visualized heatmap annotated percent variation explained using extractEigen() PlotEigenHeatmap(). can identify sample--sample differences.
code: pc1_eigen <- extractEigen(object = obj,                           component = "PC1") head(pc1_eigen) #>     Gene  EigenVector      PctVar #> 1   THY1  0.150266440 2.258000304 #> 2   CCL2  0.135706807 1.841633753 #> 3   SSX1 -0.130106138 1.692760703 #> 4 AKR1C2 -0.116614608 1.359896690 #> 5   GPX1  0.111588141 1.245191327 #> 6 MYL12B  0.005002684 0.002502684   hm2 <- PlotEigenHeatmap(obj,                  pc = "PC1",                  n = 25,                  annotate_by = "Genotype",                  annotate_colors = colorList) hm2$heatmap # GenSave(hm2, "/path/to/EuclidenDistance_Heatmap.png", width = 6, height = 8)

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: interpret principal components, individual PCs can correlated sample metadata using PlotEigenCorr(). function computes Pearson correlations displays heatmap, helping reveal metadata features associated major axes variation. Categorical variables two levels (Genotype) use Pearson correlation; categorical variables two levels (batch) summarized unsigned multiple correlation R one-way linear model, results depend levels labelled. Variables tested, columns single value unique value per sample (, Disease, CellLine_CellType, Sample), dropped. function returns list 4 elements: • $cor_matrix (Pearson correlation values, multiple correlation R variables two levels) • $pval_matrix (Associated correlation p-values) • $stars (asterisk representations p-values) • $plot (Eigencorr plot, ggplot2 object, can saved ggsave) Note: PlotOrdCorr() can used microbiome data correlates metadata features NMDS beta values rather PCs.
code: ec <- PlotEigenCorr(obj, num_pcs = 5) ec$plot

title: RGenEDA Tutorial
text: Differentially expressed genes can now stored RGenEDA object. RGenEDA designed directly work DEG tables derived DESeq2 contain column names “baseMean”, “log2FoldChange” “padj”. DEG tables packages can used minor dataframe manipulation. Note: multiple DEG assays can appended DEGs slot passing assay name SetDEGs() command (example, raw DESeq2 results Shrunk DESeq2 results.) get quick diagnosis differential expression results, histogram un-corrected pvalues can plotted using PlotPValHist().  quickly summarize DEG results different thresholds, run SummarizeDEGs(). function can take multiple assays needed outputs results tabular format. DEG assays can filtered directly saved new assay DEGs slot using FilterDEGs() Basic DEG visualizations plots MA plots volcano plots can plotted using PlotMA() PlotVolcano() “Num” “Den” arguments refer numerator level denominator level (reference level experiment, case, “WT”)  volcano plot specifying numerator denominator (denominator comparison reference level).  get glance everything , can plot differential expression dashboard DEDashboard()  explore whether differentially expressed gene (DEG) also highly variable gene (HVG), intersect two vectors can taken obtain highly variable DEGs (hvDEGs), can useful applications gene-set variation analysis (GSVA). obtain , FindHVDEGs() function can used. direction fold change intersect HVGs can either “positive”, “negative”, returns vector genes, “” contains list $positive, $negative, $slots.

what: Plot Eigen-Correlation With Metadata Heatmap — PlotEigenCorr
title: Plot Eigen-Correlation With Metadata Heatmap — PlotEigenCorr
text: Calculate Eigen-correlations geneda object plot publication-quality heatmap using ggplot2 numeric labels significance stars. continuous variables, Pearson correlation used. P values follow convention: p < 0.001, p < 0.01, p < 0.05 = three, two, one stars, respectively. Two-level categorical variables coded factor level order, sign correlation follows level order. Categorical variables two levels summarized multiple correlation R (square root R^2 one-way linear model, score ~ variable). R unsigned (0 1) p-value comes model F-test, results depend levels labelled. Variables tested (single level, constant values, residual degrees freedom, e.g. sample ID column) dropped. Requires PCA scores DimReduction(object); recompute PCA.
